themes_detail.label: Taxi complaint surge
themes_detail.summary: Taxi complaints spiked to 12 last week versus a 4.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 182% increase (z-score: 7.11)—suggesting a sudden deterioration in for-hire vehicle service quality or enforcement in Lower East Side/Chinatown this week.
evidence: 12 taxi complaints last week vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (182% spike, z-score 7.11)
For Hire Vehicle Complaint category also in top 10 by volume (581 complaints over 90 days)
This represents the most recent and sharpest spike in the dataset
reporting_angles: Interview taxi drivers and riders about what changed last week—new enforcement action, surge in unlicensed vehicles, or driver behavior shift?
Cross-check with TLC data on medallion activity, inspections, or complaints filed directly with regulators during the same period

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure damage spike
themes_detail.summary: Street Sign - Damaged complaints hit 3 last week versus 0.5 weekly average—a 500% spike (z-score: 5.0)—coinciding with broader infrastructure degradation signals, though this week's freshness is less clear than taxi complaints.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 5.0)
Bike Rack complaints also spiked 967% (4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 avg, z-score 5.21)
701 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (590 alterations, 43 new buildings, 7 demolitions) suggest active construction footprint
reporting_angles: Map damaged street signs and bike racks by location—is damage concentrated near active construction sites or a specific neighborhood block?
Interview DOT about maintenance backlog and whether construction activity is driving infrastructure damage

themes_detail.label: Illegal dumping and posting blitz
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, Illegal Dumping complaints jumped to 15 (216% spike, z-score 6.57) and Illegal Posting to 3 (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)—both statistically severe—suggesting either enforcement vacuum or coordinated littering/vandalism activity in the district.
evidence: Illegal Dumping: 15 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.8 weekly average (216% spike, z-score 6.57)
Illegal Posting: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Community Board has repeatedly budgeted for 'Improve trash removal and cleanliness' and 'Increase vacant lot cleaning'—signals long-running problem now accelerating
reporting_angles: Geomap dumping and posting hotspots—are they clustered near specific vacant lots, construction sites, or transit hubs?
Interview Sanitation Dept about why enforcement gap opened 2 weeks ago; check whether staff shortages or policy changes coincided

themes_detail.label: Building code violations explosion
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints skyrocketed 3 weeks ago to 154 versus a 15.1 weekly average—a 918% spike (z-score 4.04)—suggesting a major code enforcement action, illegal conversion wave, or inspection campaign targeting residential or commercial use violations in Lower East Side/Chinatown.
evidence: Building/Use: 154 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 15.1 weekly average (918% spike, z-score 4.04)
701 DOB permits filed in last 90 days with 590 alterations—high alteration activity may be triggering use-violation complaints
Active ULURP applications (St. Augustine's, Allen Street properties) indicate active development and potential displacement/use-conflict pressure
reporting_angles: What triggered the 154 Building/Use complaints spike 3 weeks ago—did DOB launch a targeted inspection campaign, or did residents report illegal conversions?
Investigate whether the spike correlates with the active ULURP projects and developer pressure on the neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Dead animal cleanup failure
themes_detail.summary: Dead Animal complaints hit 16 three weeks ago versus a 0.8 weekly average—a 2033% spike (z-score: 23.06, highest severity in dataset)—indicating either a public health event, rat infestation surge, or systemic cleanup failure in the district.
evidence: Dead Animal: 16 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (2033% spike, z-score 23.06—highest in entire dataset)
Encampment complaints (457 over 90 days) and Unsanitary Condition complaints (445 over 90 days) suggest overlapping sanitation crises
Community Board budget requests for 'Improve trash removal and cleanliness' indicate chronic infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks Sanitation and DEP about the dead animal spike 3 weeks ago—was it a single event (die-off) or ongoing failure?
Investigate whether the spike correlates with rat activity, food waste, or encampment-related sanitation breakdowns in specific blocks
